Mr. Mayank Deep, Advocate  Mr. Tapeshwar Nr. Thakur, Advocate For the Respondents : Mr. M. B. Lal, Advocate  ---
 rd 07/3 October 2024 1.
Learned counsel for the parties are present.

2. This writ petition has been filed for the following reliefs: -
"a.

For issuance of appropriate writ(s)/order(s)/ direction(s) particularly in the nature of Certiorari for quashing the notice issued to the petitioner vide notice dated 27.10.2020 (Annexure 5) issued under the provision of The Public Premises (Eviction Manzar Hussain @ Manjer Hussain vs Central Coal Field Limited on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92233813/
1 of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971 whereby and whereunder the petitioner has been show caused, as to why he should not be removed from the land in question which is situated at Mouza Boria, Khata No. 40, Plot NO. 635 and 638, area measuring 20 decimals out of 1.50 acres.

entities.text: Public Premises (Eviction Manzar Hussain @ Manjer Hussain vs Central Coal Field Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And/Or b.

Further the Petitioner prays for issuance of appropriate writ(s)/order(s)/direction(s) especially in the nature of mandamus for directing the respondent not to take any action in pursuance to the notice dated 27.10.2020 issued for removing the petitioner from the alleged piece of land while mentioning that the petitioner is residing there without any permission from the respondents.

Further the petitioner prays for issuance of writ(s)/ order(s)/ direction(s) specially especially a writ declaring that the land acquisition proceeding purportedly initiated vide notification dated 23.11.1957, is deemed to be lapsed as no award has been prepared nor any compensation has yet been paid to the petitioner in lieu of such acquisition and as per the terms of section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 the entire alleged acquisition proceeding is deemed to be lapsed;
And/Or e.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Further the Petitioner prays for issuance of appropriate writ(s)/order(s)/direction(s) especially a writ in the nature of mandamus for directing the respondent to pay the compensation amount and other benefits including the interest on the said compensation amount on account of fresh acquisition of land in question or alternatively the respondent authority may be restrained from making any kind of construction or alterations without making payment of adequate compensation the petitioner.

And / Or f. Further the petitioner prays for a direction that the petitioner may not be dispossessed from the land in question, as the respondent authority are forcing and taking coercive action to remove the petitioner from the land in question.
And/Or g. Such other relief/reliefs as Your Lordships may deem fit and proper to do conscionable justice to the Petitioner."

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that with respect to the same property, there was a title suit between the parties and the title was declared in favour of the petitioner and the appeal before the High Court was also decided in favour of the petitioner.
Now the respondent-CCL has filed SLP before the Hon'ble Supreme Court which is Diary No. 45163/2024 on 28.09.2024.

Manzar Hussain @ Manjer Hussain vs Central Coal Field Limited on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92233813/
2 4.

entities.text: Manzar Hussain @ Manjer Hussain vs Central Coal Field Limited on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel submits that as on date, the respondents do not have any locus to evict the petitioner from the same property under the provisions of Public Premises (Eviction of unauthorized occupants) Act.

entities.text: Public Premises (Eviction of unauthorized occupants) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He submits that the respondents may have fresh cause of action if they ultimately win before the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
5. The aforesaid history of litigation as narrated by the learned counsel for the petitioner is not disputed by the learned counsel for the respondents.
He submits that right may be reserved with the respondents to proceed afresh if the case before the Hon'ble Supreme Court is decided in favour of the respondents.

6. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Court is of the considered view that the respondents cannot proceed pursuant to impugned notice dated 27.10.2020 as the title with regard to the property is in favour of the petitioner as on date which is subject matter before the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
7. Accordingly, notice dated 27.10.2020 is hereby set-aside.
8. Liberty is reserved with the respondents to take fresh steps subject to final result of the case before the Hon'ble Supreme Court with respect to the title of the property .
9. This writ petition is hereby disposed of.
10. Pending I.A., if any, is closed.

(Anubha Rawat Choudhary, J.) Mukul Manzar Hussain @ Manjer Hussain vs Central Coal Field Limited on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92233813/
